subject.title: fix(qqbot): bind direct C2C fallback approvals to trusted actor identity

question: Which identity should authorize QQBot direct fallback approval callbacks when the user can chat but has no explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` or `execApprovals.approvers` entry?
rationale: Granting every private-chat sender approval authority weakens a privileged-operation boundary, while retaining the current rule without recovery leaves the reported workflow blocked; source inspection cannot choose that product and trust policy.

options.title: Keep explicit trust plus recovery
options.body: Retain the explicit trusted-identity requirement, treat this branch as test-only coverage, and implement visible `/bot-me` and approval-only setup guidance or automation for denied C2C callbacks.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Treat possession of a private QQ conversation as sufficient approval authority, accepting that any user permitted to chat could approve privileged operations.

options.title: Require dedicated approvers
options.body: Remove `allowFrom` as an implicit approval source and require `channels.qqbot.execApprovals.approvers`, with an upgrade and setup path for existing users.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit trust plus recovery
recommendation.body: Retain the explicit trusted-identity requirement, treat this branch as test-only coverage, and implement visible `/bot-me` and approval-only setup guidance or automation for denied C2C callbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows direct involvement in defining, fixing, verifying, and merging this exact QQBot approval authorization boundary.
